title: AI Diet Apps Count Calories Wrong — Study
paragraphs: Many people who are trying to lose weight use apps to keep track of what they eat. Some of the latest apps use artificial intelligence to estimate the calories in a meal from a single photo. However, new research suggests that these estimates may be considerably lower than the real figures.

The research was presented in July 2026 at NUTRITION 2026, the annual meeting of the American Society for Nutrition. It was led by Aaron Hengist of the National Institutes of Health, or NIH, in the United States.

The researchers used meals from a larger NIH study that compared different diets. These meals were prepared in a special kitchen where every ingredient was weighed very precisely, so the researchers knew exactly how many calories and nutrients each meal contained. They then took standard photos of 102 meals and analyzed them with four popular apps: MyFitnessPal, Lose It!, Cal AI and Appediet. Finally, they compared the apps' estimates with the actual figures.

All four apps underestimated the number of calories, by around a third on average. According to the researchers, this was mainly because the apps did not count fat correctly. The apps' estimates for carbohydrates were more consistent than those for fat or protein. In a further analysis of more than 200 additional meals, the apps performed even worse on low-carbohydrate, high-fat meals, known as ketogenic meals.

Hengist warned that "These apps tend to underestimate calories, especially from fats." He therefore advised people who rely on photos without adjusting portion sizes or entering amounts themselves to be careful, because they are probably eating more than the app suggests.

However, the study has some limitations. It has not yet been peer-reviewed, so the results are preliminary. In addition, it tested only four apps and meals from a single study, so the findings may not apply to other apps or everyday meals. The researchers suggest that combining photo-based apps with traditional methods may improve accuracy.
